source_text: Tunc dixit mihi frater meus: Domina soror, iam in magna dignatione es: tanta es ut postules uisionem et ostendatur tibi an passio sit an commeatus. Et ego quae me sciebam fabulari cum domino, cuius beneficia tanta experta eram, fidens repromisi ei dicens: Crastina die tibi renuntiabo. Et postulaui, et ostensum est mihi hoc. Uideo scalam aeream mirae longitudinis, pertingentem usque ad caelum, et angustam, per quam nonnisi singuli ascendere possent; et in lateribus scalae omne genus ferramentorum infixum erat ibi: gladii, lanceae, hami, macherae, ueruta: ut, si quis neglegenter aut non sursum adtendens ascenderet, laniaretur et carnes eius inhaererent ferramentis. Et erat sub ipsa scala draco cubans mirae magnitudinis, qui ascendentibus insidias praestabat et exterrebat ne ascenderent. Ascendit autem Saturus prior, qui postea se propter nos ultro tradiderat, quia ipse nos aedificauerat; et tunc cum adducti sumus praesens non fuerat. Et peruenit in caput scalae, et conuertit se et dixit mihi: Perpetua, sustineo te; sed uide ne te mordeat draco ille. Et dixi ego: Non me nocebit, in nomine Iesu Christi. Et desub ipsa scala, quasi timens me, lente eiecit caput; et quasi primum gradum calcarem, calcaui illi caput, et ascendi. Et uidi spatium immensum horti, et in medio sedentem hominem canum in habitu pastoris, grandem, oues mulgentem: et circumstantes candidati milia multa. Et leuauit caput et aspexit me et dixit mihi: Bene uenisti, tegnon. Et clamauit me, et de caseo quod mulgebat dedit mihi quasi buccellam; et ego accepi iunctis manibus et manducaui; et uniuersi circumstantes dixerunt: Amen. Et ad sonum uocis experrecta sum, commanducans adhuc dulce nescio quid. Et retuli statim fratri meo, et intelleximus passionem esse futuram; et coepi iam nullam spem in saeculo habere.
thought_title: The ladder, the dragon, and the shepherd
orientation: Perpetua herself is speaking in her prison diary and reports the first vision she asked for about her coming fate.
pass_a_gloss: Then my brother said to me: Lady sister, now you are in great favor: you are so great that you may ask for a vision and it may be shown to you whether it is martyrdom or release. And I who knew that I was talking with the Lord, whose so great benefits I had experienced, confidently promised him saying: Tomorrow I will report back to you. And I asked, and this was shown to me. I see a bronze ladder of wonderful length, reaching all the way to heaven, and narrow, through which only one by one could go up; and on the sides of the ladder every kind of iron tool had been fastened there: swords, spears, hooks, knives, javelins: so that, if anyone went up carelessly or not looking upward, he would be torn and his flesh would stick on the iron tools. And there was under the ladder itself a dragon lying of wonderful size, who set an ambush for those going up and frightened them so that they would not go up. But Saturus went up first, who afterwards for our sake had handed himself over of his own accord, because he himself had built us up; and at that time when we were arrested he had not been present. And he arrived at the head of the ladder, and he turned and said to me: Perpetua, I am waiting for you; but see that that dragon does not bite you. And I said: He will not hurt me, in the name of Jesus Christ. And from under the ladder itself, as if fearing me, slowly he put out his head; and as if I were treading the first step, I trod on his head, and I went up. And I saw an immense open space of garden, and in the middle sitting a white-haired man in shepherd's dress, large, milking sheep: and standing around him white-clad ones many thousands. And he lifted his head and looked at me and said to me: You have come well, child. And he called me, and from the cheese which he was milking he gave to me as it were a little morsel; and I received with joined hands and I ate; and all those standing around said: Amen. And at the sound of the voice I awoke, still chewing something sweet I do not know what. And I reported at once to my brother, and we understood that martyrdom was to be in the future; and I began now to have no hope in the world.

lemmas.gloss: to wait for or hold out for someone

choices.why: brief glossary fixes visio as vision as promised revelation
passio is fixed as martyrdom and commeatus is its opposite outcome from arrest, not pardon in general
Saturus has already gone up and looks back, so the sense is waiting, not enduring
Greek vocative kept in Latin letters for the shepherd's address; rendered in normal English

choices.english: something sweet I do not know what
choices.why: keeps indefinite nescio quid and neuter adjective force on waking

pass_b_english: Then my brother said to me, "My lady sister, you stand high in favor now: you are great enough to ask for a vision, and it will be shown to you whether this means martyrdom or release." I knew that I talked with the Lord, and I had come to know such great kindness from him, so I promised him with confidence, "I will tell you tomorrow." I asked, and this is what was shown to me.

I see a bronze ladder of astonishing length, reaching all the way to heaven. It was narrow, and only one person at a time could climb it. Every kind of iron blade was fixed to its sides: swords, spears, hooks, knives, and javelins, so that anyone who climbed carelessly and without looking upward would be torn, and pieces of flesh would catch on the blades. A dragon of astonishing size lay coiled directly beneath the ladder. It laid ambushes for those climbing and terrified them so that they would not climb. Saturus climbed first. He later gave himself up for us of his own accord, because he had built us up, and he had not been present when we were arrested. He reached the top of the ladder, turned, and said to me, "Perpetua, I am waiting for you. But watch that the dragon does not bite you." I answered, "He will not harm me, in the name of Jesus Christ." As if it feared me, the dragon slowly thrust its head out from beneath the ladder, and as I set foot on the first rung, I stepped on its head and climbed up.

I saw a vast expanse of garden, and in the middle sat a white-haired man of great stature, dressed like a shepherd and milking sheep, with many thousands in white robes standing around him. He raised his head, looked at me, and said to me, "Welcome, child." He called me to him and gave me a mouthful of the cheese he was making from the milk. I took it in cupped hands and ate it, and all those standing around said, "Amen." At the sound of the voice I woke, still chewing something sweet I could not name. I told my brother at once, and we understood that martyrdom lay ahead. From that moment I began to have no hope left in this world.
notes: tegnon spells Greek teknon in Latin letters; sense as shepherd's address is clear but exact transliteration is uncertain.
commanducans is an intensive or late form for chewing; glossed from context of eating the morsel on waking.
